title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Vertex Analytics
next_steps: Send POC proposal and pricing by 2025-02-18
Share security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts
Schedule benchmark run for week of 2025-02-24
Follow up on data residency question with infra team by 2025-02-17
action_items: Sofia Martinez - Draft POC SOW and pricing - due 2025-02-18
Ethan Cho - Prep benchmark script and perf checklist - due 2025-02-21
Daniel Kim - Share sample anonymized workload and current qps numbers - due 2025-02-17
Priya Desai - Confirm success criteria and ML eval rubric - due 2025-02-18
transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-02-14 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Vertex Head of ML), Mark Hollis (CTO), Daniel Kim (Infra Eng)

Summary: Quick POC scoping to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Need benchmarks (latency/cost/QPS), success criteria (latency SLOs, accuracy regressions), timeline for 4-week POC and stakeholders. Security and VPC/data residency blockers discussed.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time, I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Ethan our systems engineer. quick 45 min agenda: confirm goals, sizing, constraints, and next steps for a POC. Priya: yep sounds good.
[01:12] Ethan: Can you give us a sense of your workload — is it synchronous chat, batch embeddings, or a mix?
[01:25] Priya: Mostly real-time chat ops inside our analytics platform, around 200 qps at peak for the assistant, and then nightly batch for embeddings, maybe 40k docs a night. latency target is 200 to 300 ms p95 for chat. cost is tight; we're a mid-market team. 
[02:40] Mark: We also have data residency concerns, some EU and US customers; need audit logs and KMS integration. SOC two compliance is a must.
[03:05] Ethan: Got it. For that latency you might consider either Dedicated or Hosted with edge routing, depends on tail latencies and caching. Our hosted API can hit low latencies for many workloads but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. 
[04:00] Daniel: What's the difference operationally? we prefer not to manage infra but if we go private we can keep everything on-prem.
[04:20] Sofia: Right, short version: Hosted = fastest to start, pay-per-use, Redwood manages everything. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for you, predictable throughput and can be in VPC; Private = customer-managed control plane, on-prem option, full isolation and KMS integration. 
[05:01] Priya: Our main decision factors are: 1) p95 latency under load 2) model output quality matched to our benchmarks 3) cost per 1M tokens 4) security controls (KMS, audit logs) 5) timeline — we want a vendor in production in Q2 if possible.
[06:30] Ethan: Ok for the POC we usually run a 3 to 4 week cycle: week 0 onboarding and credentialing, week 1 smoke tests and baseline hosted runs, week 2 dedicated sizing/benchmarks or private deployment (if needed), week 3 final validation and handoff. We can compress to 3 weeks if decisions are clear.
[07:50] Mark: We have an internal procurement window at end of March, so timeline aligns. Who owns infra setup for Dedicated? 
[08:10] Ethan: Redwood will provision Dedicated pools and support network setup; for VPC peering you need your infra team to approve firewall rules. For Private on-prem we share an install bundle but your ops run it, we support remotely.
[09:00] Daniel: On the sizing note, our current assistant model is a 7B variant running in-house quantized to 4bit for cost. We expect average token length 120, peak concurrent sessions ~90. 
[09:30] Sofia: Great data point. For benchmarking we'll ask you to send a sample trace plus a synthetic load generator. For Dedicated sizing we typically map that to N GPUs using our throughput targets e.g., a single A100-80GB equiv can handle X qps under batching — Ethan can share the sizing table.
[10:45] Ethan: I'll share a preliminary sizing table; rough rule: with batching and KV cache used we often get 3-5x throughput relative to naive runs, but it depends on sequence lengths and hit rates. Also note quantization/ops change things — sometimes 4bit gives great perf but may have slightly different quality.
[12:02] Priya: Are there feature limitations on Hosted? e.g., can we do private models or custom tokenization? 
[12:20] Sofia: Hosted supports private model uploads and custom prompt templates; for strict data residency or air-gapped needs Private is recommended. Hosted does have usage logs and customer-level RBAC, but if you need single-tenant encryption we move to Dedicated or Private.
[13:10] Mark: About metrics — we need token-level cost break down and per-route dashboards, can we see that during POC?
[13:33] Ethan: Yes we can grant access to Redwood Console where you can see cost and latency per route; we'll include tracing hooks for a few sample requests.
[14:00] Priya: For success criteria we'll measure: p95 latency under 80% load <= 300ms, accuracy delta vs baseline < 2% on our eval set, and cost per 1M tokens <= $XX (TBD by finance).
[15:20] Sofia: noted. We'll capture that in the SOW. Also propose a bench where we run hosted first as baseline, then Dedicated to compare cost/perf and optionally Private if the security team requires it.
[16:35] Daniel: If we run hosted baseline, do you have guaranteed SLOs? we need to be comfortable that spikes won't break SLAs in prod.
[16:50] Ethan: Hosted has metrics and soft SLAs but for contractual SLA-backed uptime and latency guarantees we go with Dedicated and an enterprise agreement. Hosted is operationally simpler but less contractual.
[17:30] Priya: For benchmarks, can Redwood run the same model variants with 4bit quant and fp16 to compare quality vs perf?
[17:44] Ethan: Yes, we'll run both quantized and fp16 variants. If you share the model or use a Redwood-verified open model we can reproduce. There may be small differences in output tokens from quant and you should include your eval set to measure regressions.
[19:10] Mark: Who pays for Dedicated during POC? is there an eval credit program?
[19:25] Sofia: We can provide credits for hosted runs and offer a reduced short-term reserved capacity agreement for Dedicated POCs. We'll outline options in the proposal.
[20:02] Priya: Data residency — some EU customers require data to never leave EU. How does that work for Hosted?
[20:18] Ethan: We can route requests to EU regions and store logs in-region, but for strict legal requirements the Private on-prem or VPC-backed Dedicated with EU-only hardware might be required. We'll check region availability.
[21:45] Daniel: Network setup: for Dedicated we need VPC peering, firewall rules and maybe a transit gateway. That will take 3-5 biz days from our networking team.
[22:20] Sofia: We'll coordinate timing. For the POC we recommend starting with Hosted baseline to get quick numbers while infra approvals are processed for Dedicated/VPC.
[23:50] Priya: Can we run an offline embedding batch in your hosted environment? we need to see throughput for 40k docs nightly.
[24:05] Ethan: Yes, batch embeddings run fine in hosted; we'll show throughput and cost estimates. For heavy nightly batch you might prefer Dedicated to compress window and control costs.
[25:40] Sofia: On security, we'll send the SOC2 doc, pen-test summary, and KMS integration guide. Any non-standard compliance needs?
[26:10] Mark: We might need ISO27001 attestation as well. Also SAML SSO into Redwood Console.
[26:35] Ethan: SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs are supported; we'll include the docs and ask infra for expected metadata.
[27:40] Priya: For the POC evaluation rubric we have automated tests for hallucination rate, answer relevance, and latency under synthetic load. We'll share the rubric.
[28:05] Sofia: Perfect — once we have that we can map pass/fail thresholds to POC success.
[29:30] Daniel: For the benchmark harness, please share what metrics you collect — CPU/GPU utilization, per-token latency, KV cache hit rate etc.
[29:48] Ethan: We'll provide a perf checklist including GPU utilization, memory, token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and KV cache hit rates.
[31:10] Priya: If Dedicated is better on cost per token but needs a monthly commit, how flexible are burst options?
[31:28] Sofia: Dedicated has burst capacity options and autoscaling policies; we can add short-term burst capacity for spikes. We'll include pricing tiers in the proposal.
[32:55] Mark: Timeline recap?
[33:05] Sofia: Suggested: by 2025-02-17 we exchange sample traces and SSO metadata; by 2025-02-18 Redwood sends draft SOW and pricing; week of 2025-02-24 run hosted baseline benchmarks; week of 2025-03-03 run Dedicated sizing/benchmarks (if infra approved); final evaluation by 2025-03-14 to align with procurement.
[34:40] Priya: That works. Also can you show us a quick example of the console dashboards after the call?
[34:55] Ethan: Sure I can share a recording/demo and grant a read-only view. I'll drop links.
[35:40] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) question about model rollouts and canaries
[35:50] Ethan: Rollouts are supported — canary, A/B and automatic fallback to smaller models on degradation. We'll show rollout controls in the console.
[36:22] Priya: Pricing detail request — need cost per 1M tokens for hosted and a committed monthly price for Dedicated (for 3 and 12 month terms).
[36:40] Sofia: We'll include those in the SOW; finance will include scenarios based on your token estimates.
[37:15] Mark: One more security Q — audit logs retention, can we set retention policy and export logs to our SIEM?
[37:30] Ethan: Yes, logs can be exported to S3 or SIEM via syslog/forwarders and retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has default retention but enterprise add-on gives longer retention.
[38:45] Priya: Great, any blockers from Redwood side to start baseline hosted testing this week?
[39:00] Sofia: No blockers; if you share credentials and sample traces we'll spin up endpoints and a test project.
[39:30] Daniel: We'll turn around traces by EOD tomorrow.
[40:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll send the SOW and security docs by Tuesday. Recap of next steps: ship SOW, share benchmark harness, schedule baseline run.
[41:20] Priya: Thanks all.
[41:35] Sofia: End call.

References: link: https://redwood.example.com/proposal/CRM-32458 (proposal stub), link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/security/soc2.pdf (SOC2), link: https://redwood.example.com/console-demo (console demo recording)

Action items (short): Sofia to send SOW; Ethan to share sizing table and benchmark script; Daniel to send sample traces; Priya to share eval rubric.
